features.claim: It had four flippers instead of legs.
features.quote: Like all plesiosaurs, Kronosaurus has four paddle-like limbs, a short tail and, like most pliosaurids, a long head and a short neck.

features.claim: Its head was long and its neck was short.
features.quote: Like all plesiosaurs, Kronosaurus has four paddle-like limbs, a short tail and, like most pliosaurids, a long head and a short neck.
Like all plesiosaurs, Kronosaurus has four paddle-like limbs, a short tail and, like most pliosaurids, a long head and a short neck.

features.claim: The front of its skull stretched out into a snout.
features.quote: The front of the skull is elongated into a rostrum (snout).

features.claim: Its teeth were big and cone-shaped.
features.quote: The large cone-shaped teeth of Kronosaurus would have been used for a diet consisting of large prey.

features.claim: The teeth at the front of its mouth were bigger than the teeth at the back.
features.quote: The front teeth are larger than the back teeth.

features.claim: Its back flippers were bigger than its front flippers.
features.quote: The limbs of Kronosaurus were modified into flippers, with the back pair larger than the front.

features.claim: Its flippers could spread wider than five metres across.
features.quote: The flippers would have given a wingspan of more than 5 m (16 ft) for the largest representatives.

features.claim: Its lower jaws joined together in a long, spoon-shaped front part.
features.quote: The mandibular symphysis of Kronosaurus is elongated and spatulate (spoon-shaped), and like its close relatives Brachauchenius and Megacephalosaurus, it contains up to six pairs of teeth.
Like all plesiosaurs, it had a short tail, a massive trunk and two pairs of large flippers.

features.claim: It was probably about nine to eleven metres long.
features.quote: Its true length was probably only 9–10.9 meters (30–36 feet).

features.claim: Its hind limbs were longer than its forelimbs.
features.quote: The hindlimbs of Kronosaurus are longer than its forelimbs, with the femur being longer and more robust than the humerus.

not_this.claim: Old pictures made it much longer than it really was.
not_this.quote: The Harvard reconstruction may have included too many vertebrae, exaggerating its length.

not_this.claim: The old Harvard skeleton was rebuilt with too many back bones.
not_this.quote: According to Australian paleontologist Colin McHenry, the specimen has eight extra vertebrae added to the spine and the skull is not supposed to have a bulbous shaped sagittal crest on top.

not_this.claim: The old skeleton was put together with the wrong proportions.
not_this.quote: In addition, it seems that the skeleton was reconstructed with the wrong proportions.

debated.claim: Scientists are not sure how big it really was.
debated.quote: Kronosaurus is one of the largest pliosaurs identified to date, but several estimates as to its exact size have been proposed during research.

debated.claim: The shape of the top of its skull is uncertain because that part was rebuilt in plaster.
debated.quote: However, as White indicates in his description of the specimen in 1935, much of the skull roof is not preserved and is mostly restored in plaster, the real proportions being therefore uncertain.

debated.claim: The real fossil bones are hard to see because so much plaster was added.
debated.quote: However, as the latter was massively restored in plaster, it is currently difficult to discern the real fossil material.

debated.claim: The tail is not known from complete fossil skeletons.
debated.quote: Although the tail of Kronosaurus is unknown from articulated specimens, the end of the caudal vertebrae would have supported a small caudal fin like in other plesiosaurs.
